title.heading:
Motor, ESC and
servo test bench
title.text:
A 7 inch touch panel and an RP2350 IOmcu,
linked by CAN at 1 Mbit/s.

labels.title: Case
labels.text: Holds every board. Closed at the back.

labels.title: Emergency stop
labels.text: M16 button on the back wall.

labels.title: PD mini
labels.text: USB-PD supply for the servo rails, set from the panel.

labels.title: rbmod carrier
labels.text: Fixes every lead of the IOmcu to a pin.

labels.title: 5 V converters
labels.text: For the programming ports and the module.

labels.title: J1 · programming ports
labels.text: 4 positions with a fixed 5 V, for the servo programmers.

say.text: This is R C bench: a test bench for motors, ESCs and servos.
Then the emergency stop, the X T 60 socket, and the U S B C socket for power.
The P D mini is the supply for the servo rails.
The R B mod carrier brings the I O M C U, a current monitor, two 5 volt converters and the U S B P D trigger.
Last comes the touch panel: a seven inch display on an E S P 32 P 4.
On the connector wall, J 2 carries the outputs for servos and speed controllers, and J 1 the four programming ports.

steps.title: Start-up check
steps.text: The panel reports board, display, touch, storage, settings, link and IOmcu before the home screen.

steps.title: One home screen
steps.text: Each function of the bench opens from one of eight tiles.

steps.title: STOP on one touch
steps.text: STOP latches at first contact. Motor and servo outputs and the supply go off.
points: A heartbeat line and a link watchdog disable the outputs
A 2 s hold on STOP resets it
steps.say: Stop on one touch. Stop latches at first contact: motor and servo outputs and the supply go off. Arming takes a two second hold.

steps.title: Faults in plain words
steps.text: A tap on the fault chip names each cause and what to check.

steps.title: CAN bus test
steps.text: Test frames run at start. A failed test lists what to check on the wiring.
steps.say: CAN bus test. Test frames run at start. A failed test lists what to check on the wiring.

card.title: Motor & ESC
card.text: Run a motor, read its telemetry, program its ESC.

steps.say: Chapter 2. Motor and electronic speed controller. Run a motor, read its telemetry, and program its controller.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.text: The first tile of the home screen.

steps.title: Live telemetry
steps.text: Voltage, current, power and rpm, plotted while the motor runs.
points: Speed and ESC temperature from bidirectional DShot
Each run is logged as a CSV file
steps.say: Live telemetry. This screen runs a motor and shows what it draws: voltage, current, power and rpm, plotted while it runs. Each run is logged.

steps.title: Bench against ESC
steps.text: The table sets the bench's own readings beside what the ESC reports.
steps.say: Bench against controller. The table compares the bench's own measurements with what the controller reports, so you see how far its telemetry is off.

steps.title: Pack and motor data
steps.text: Cells, capacity and internal resistance of the pack. Pole count and rated kV of the motor.
steps.say: Pack and motor data. Enter the pack's cells and capacity and the motor's pole count, so the bench can work out rpm and the remaining charge.

steps.title: Stick programming
steps.text: Many ESCs are set up with the throttle stick, while they beep through a menu. The bench knows these menus for 74 ESC families.
steps.say: Stick programming. Many speed controllers are set up with the throttle stick: you move it while the controller beeps through a menu. The bench knows these menus for 74 families of controllers.

steps.title: Menu items
steps.text: You choose the settings on the panel instead of counting beeps.
steps.say: Menu items. Instead of counting beeps yourself, you choose the settings on the panel, for example brake or cutoff mode.

steps.title: The run
steps.text: The bench moves the throttle for you and steps through the ESC's menu until every item is set.
steps.say: The run. The bench then moves the throttle for you at the right moments, and steps through the menu until every item is set.

steps.title: ESC signal wire
steps.text: AM32, Bluejay, BLHeli_S and ESCape32: settings are read, edited and written through the signal wire.
steps.say: The signal wire. Newer controller firmware, such as AM32, Bluejay, BLHeli_S and ESCape32, is set up through the signal wire instead. The bench reads the settings, lets you edit them, and writes them back.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.text: The second tile. Servos plug into J2, programmed servos into J1.

steps.title: Eight servo tools
steps.text: Tester, sweep, automatic test, limit run, rudder gauge and two programmers.

steps.title: LIVE
steps.text: A servo tester: a dial commands the position while the bench is ARMED.
steps.say: Live. A servo tester: a dial commands the position, and the screen shows the pulse, the measured angle, and the current the servo draws.

steps.title: SWEEP
steps.text: A square, sine or triangle sweep, timed by the IOmcu, with speed and pause.
steps.say: Sweep. Moves the servo back and forth on its own, as a square, sine or triangle, at a set speed and pause.

steps.title: Servo type and pulses
steps.text: Type, frame rate, pulse minimum, centre and maximum, and trim.

steps.title: A hold before a risk
steps.text: A type that can destroy a servo opens a warning. It applies after a 2 s hold.

steps.title: HV servos only
steps.text: An output above 6.0 V asks for a 2 s hold as well.

steps.title: TEST
steps.text: An automatic test steps the supply from 4.8 to 6.0 V and looks for the brown-out.
points: Travel time and hold current per step
A CSV file and a text report on the card
steps.say: Test. An automatic test shows how a servo behaves as its supply drops. It steps the voltage from 4.8 to 6.0 volts, measures travel time and current, and looks for the brown-out. It writes a report to the card.

steps.title: Test steps
steps.text: 4.8 V and 6.0 V steps, 7.4 V and 8.4 V with HV SERVO on, and a brown-out search in 0.20 V steps.
steps.say: Test steps. 4.8 and 6.0 volts; 7.4 and 8.4 volts for high voltage servos; and a brown-out search in steps of 0.2 volts.

steps.title: LIMIT RUN
steps.text: For an installed servo: finds where the linkage stops at each end, from the servo's current.
steps.say: Limit run. For a servo that is installed in a model: the bench moves it towards each end and finds where the linkage stops, from the servo's current. That gives the travel you can use.

steps.title: SEARCH + PROGRAM
steps.text: The ends found are written into a KST, Chaservo or Hitec servo on the programming port.

steps.title: RUDDER
steps.text: A deflection gauge: degrees, and mm at the trailing edge, from the surface's length.
steps.say: Rudder. A deflection gauge: it shows how far a control surface moves, in degrees, and in millimetres at the trailing edge.

steps.title: Angle source
steps.text: The AS5600 encoder on the horn or a Bluetooth IMU on the surface.

steps.title: RUDDER AUTO
steps.text: Programs a servo's end points for a set deflection, on the programming port.
steps.say: Rudder Auto. Set the deflection you want, and it programs the servo's end points to match, on the programming port.

steps.title: KST and Chaservo
steps.text: The programmer reads 32 registers over the signal wire.
points: Edits are a draft until WRITE
Backup to the card before the first write
Every written value is read back
steps.say: KST and Chaservo. A programmer for these servos: it reads their 32 registers over the signal wire, with settings such as dead band, travel and failsafe. Edits stay a draft until you write them.

steps.title: Servo files
steps.text: A servo's settings are saved to the card and loaded into another servo of the same type.

steps.title: RESTORE
steps.text: The session's first read is kept as a backup. A restore writes it back.

steps.title: An interrupted write
steps.text: A write that did not finish is detected at the next read. The screen says so and offers RESTORE.

steps.title: Hitec
steps.text: D series and classic HS-5xxx and HS-7xxx servos, with backup, limit checks and a write switch.
steps.say: Hitec. The same for Hitec's D series and classic digital servos, with backup, limit checks and a write switch.

steps.title: Backup and verify
steps.text: The session's backup file is named on the screen. Written values are read back.

card.title: Supply
card.text: A USB-PD supply, set from the panel.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.text: The third tile. The PD mini feeds the servo rails on J2.

steps.title: USB-PD supply
steps.text: Voltage and current limit of the PD mini are set on the panel. PROG 5V switches the programming ports' own 5 V.
points: V, A and W plotted and logged

marks.text: Plot of V, A and W

steps.say: U S B P D supply. Voltage and current limit of the P D mini are set on the panel. Prog 5 volt switches the programming ports' own supply.

steps.title: Where they are
steps.text: The lower row: RECEIVER, BATTERY and BALANCE are in development.

steps.title: RECEIVER
steps.text: In development.

steps.title: BATTERY
steps.text: In development.

steps.title: BALANCE
steps.text: In development.

card.title: Logs & files
card.text: Every run on the SD card.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.text: The fourth tile. FILES opens from LOGS and from SETUP.

steps.title: LOGS
steps.text: Runs are recorded to the SD card while the bench is ARMED or the supply's output is on.

steps.title: Plot on the panel
steps.text: A CSV file opens as a plot. A cursor steps through its samples.

steps.title: Import
steps.text: A CSV file from elsewhere: separator, number format and time axis are detected and can be changed.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: A test or a limit run writes a text report beside its CSV file.

steps.title: FILES
steps.text: The card in two panes: copy, move, rename, delete, new folders and text files.
points: Writes only while the bench is SAFE
The bench's own folders are protected
steps.say: Files. The card in two panes: copy, move, rename and delete, and new folders and text files.

steps.title: File information
steps.text: Name, folder, kind, size, date and the rule that protects it.

steps.title: Text editor
steps.text: Text files on the card are viewed and edited on the panel.

steps.title: Screenshot
steps.text: A 1 s hold on the empty part of the band saves the screen as a PNG file on the card.
steps.say: Screenshot. A one second hold on the empty part of the band saves the screen to the card.

card.title: Wi-Fi & updates
card.text: Files to a browser, firmware to the bench.

steps.title: Where they are
steps.text: Two tiles of SETUP: WI-FI and UPDATES.

steps.title: Access point
steps.text: The panel opens its own network: WPA2, 2.4 GHz channel 6, with a random password and an access code.
steps.say: Access point. The panel opens its own network, with a random password and an access code.

steps.title: Wi-Fi
steps.text: A browser downloads any file of the card, or the whole card as one ZIP file, and uploads panel firmware.
points: Own access point or a saved home network
Radio on only while the screen is open and for update checks
steps.say: Wi-Fi. A browser downloads any file of the card, or the whole card as one zip file, and uploads panel firmware.

steps.title: Browser writes
steps.text: Writes from the browser to the card are opened on the panel and can be shut again there.

steps.title: Panel update
steps.text: An uploaded or downloaded image is written after a 2 s hold on the panel.

steps.title: UPDATES
steps.text: The panel asks GitHub for a newer release, downloads it over HTTPS and installs it on a 2 s hold.
points: The IOmcu is updated from the panel over CAN
steps.say: Updates. The panel asks GitHub for a newer release, downloads it, and installs it on a two second hold.

steps.title: IOmcu update
steps.text: The panel sends the IOmcu image it carries over CAN. Outputs are off until the new firmware is checked.

steps.title: Radio update
steps.text: The ESP32-C6 that carries Wi-Fi and Bluetooth is updated from the panel too.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.text: The last tile of the home screen.

steps.title: SETUP
steps.text: Panel, sensors, outputs, SD card, Wi-Fi, updates, the Bluetooth IMU and the carrier's layout.

steps.title: PANEL
steps.text: Theme, brightness, contrast, screen rotation by 180° and language.

steps.title: Clock and knob
steps.text: Time zone, dim after, and a rotary knob that turns the active slider.

steps.title: SD CARD
steps.text: Which logs are written, their folders, and whether a browser may write.

steps.title: OUTPUTS
steps.text: A protocol for each pin of J2: servo PWM, motor PWM or DShot.

steps.title: LAYOUT
steps.text: On the rbmod carrier: J1 and J2 position by position, with the protocol bound on each.

steps.title: SENSORS
steps.text: The carrier's INA3221 current monitor, the AS5600 angle encoder, the phase tap and the IMU.

steps.title: Phase tap
steps.text: Listens to an ESC's beeps on one motor phase: lowest and highest tone, pitch split and gap.
steps.say: Phase tap. A wire on one motor phase lets the bench hear a controller's beeps. These settings set what counts as a beep.

steps.title: Find a sensor
steps.text: A scan lists the Bluetooth sensors in range. A tap binds one.

steps.title: Bluetooth IMU
steps.text: An angle sensor on the control surface, read over Bluetooth at 50 Hz.

steps.title: The screen guide
steps.text: The ? in the band numbers the controls of a screen and explains each.
steps.say: The screen guide. The question mark in the band numbers the controls of a screen and explains each.

steps.title: English and German
steps.text: The interface language is set on the panel.
steps.say: English and German. The interface language is set on the panel.

steps.title: Dark and light theme
steps.text: Both themes are stored with the settings.

scenes.heading: rcbench
scenes.say: That is R C bench. Its source and documentation are on GitHub.
